claims.claim: American operates a major network air carrier serving over three hundred fifty destinations and carried over two hundred twenty‑four million passengers in the most recent year, while adding more than sixty new routes.
claims.quote: Together with our wholly‑owned regional airline subsidiaries and third‑party regional carriers operating as American Eagle, our primary business activity is the operation of a major network air carrier, providing scheduled air transportation for passengers and cargo through our hubs in Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Philadelphia, Phoenix and Washington, D.C. and partner gateways, including in London, Doha, Madrid, Seattle/Tacoma, Sydney and Tokyo (among others). We provide service to over 350 destinations around the world, and in 2025, approximately 224 million passengers boarded our flights. In 2025, we launched more than 60 new routes, including to trans‑Atlantic destinations such as Spain, Italy and Greece. We also announced over 20 new routes for customers to explore in 2026, including our first trans‑Atlantic route to be flown by the Airbus A321XLR from New York to Edinburgh, Scotland.

claims.claim: The airline faces a highly competitive environment across all its markets.
claims.quote: The markets in which we operate are highly competitive.

claims.claim: Management says its investments in connectivity, lounges, seatback entertainment, airport facilities and fleet modernization are intended to build a best‑in‑class customer experience.
claims.quote: American’s investments in high‑speed connectivity, lounges, seatback entertainment, airport facilities and fleet modernization are creating the foundation for a best‑in‑class customer experience.

claims.claim: The company announced a plan to outfit more than five hundred aircraft with high‑speed Starlink Wi‑Fi, the largest in‑flight connectivity upgrade in its history.
claims.quote: In May, American announced plans to equip more than 500 aircraft with high‑speed Starlink Wi‑Fi, representing the largest in‑flight connectivity upgrade in the airline’s history.

claims.claim: American has invested in ZeroAvia’s hydrogen‑fuel‑cell technology and is working to retrofit existing FAA‑certified aircraft, a strategy aimed at simplifying regulation and shortening time to market.
claims.quote: ZeroAvia’s technology uses green hydrogen to produce electricity through a catalytic chemical reaction, which then powers the motors of the aircraft. ZeroAvia is working to retrofit and linefit its powertrains to existing FAA‑certified fixed‑wing aircraft, a strategy aimed at simplifying the regulatory process and reducing time to market.

claims.claim: The airline introduced a new premium Flagship Suite on select aircraft and announced plans to extend the offering to its larger wide‑body fleet.
claims.quote: •introduced the new premium Flagship Suite® on our Boeing 787‑9s and Airbus A321XLRs and announced plans to expand this product to our Boeing 777 fleet;

claims.claim: Management plans to expand premium seating on both new deliveries and retrofits, aiming to raise the premium seat share on narrow‑body aircraft to roughly forty percent.
claims.quote: American plans to continue expanding premium seating through the delivery of new aircraft and the retrofit of existing aircraft. Premium products generate roughly half of the company’s ticket revenue on approximately 30% of seats today. Through the recently announced narrowbody retrofit program, American expects premium seats on narrowbody aircraft to increase to 40% in the coming years.

claims.claim: Fuel cost sensitivity is highlighted; a one‑cent per gallon rise in fuel price is projected to add roughly fifty million dollars to annual fuel expense.
claims.quote: Based on our 2026 forecasted mainline and regional fuel consumption, we estimate that a one cent per gallon increase in the price of aircraft fuel would increase our 2026 annual fuel expense by approximately $50 million.

claims.claim: Management indicates ongoing and future business‑model changes intended to drive revenue growth and cost offset.
claims.quote: We have in the past instituted, and intend to institute in the future, changes to our business model designed to increase revenues and offset costs.

gaps: No specific evidence in the provided filings about the quantitative impact of the Starlink rollout on revenue or load factor; the effect remains unproven.
No disclosed timeline for the ZeroAvia retrofit beyond the current development stage; the future operational benefit is uncertain.
insight: Insight: American’s rollout of Starlink Wi‑Fi to more than five hundred aircraft marks the largest in‑flight connectivity upgrade in its history, a potential differentiator for customer experience. — EX-99.1 line 35: In May, American announced plans to equip more than 500 aircraft with high‑speed Starlink Wi‑Fi, representing the largest in‑flight connectivity upgrade in the airline’s history.
